title: An Interventional Post-Authorisation Safety Study (PASS) to further characterise the long-term safety and efficacy for subjects treated with autologous ex vivo lentiviral hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell gene therapy for Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome (WAS).
official: An Interventional Post-Authorisation Safety Study (PASS) to further characterise the long-term safety and efficacy for subjects treated with autologous ex vivo lentiviral hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell gene therapy for Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome (WAS).
summary: Main objective: - To characterize the long-term safety of etuvetidigene autotemcel treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. For patients who received GT in the clinical development program, a new EA or under Italian Law 648: 1. The patient has been treated with etuvetidigene autotemcel
2. 2. The patient or, if applicable, the patient’s parent(s)/legal guardian(s), are able and willing to provide informed consent.
3. 3. Willingness to attend the study visit schedule and be compliant with the protocol.
4. For patients treated in the commercial setting: 1. Male or female
5. 2. Patient is eligible to receive etuvetidigene autotemcel as per indication specified in SmPC/USPI
6. 3. the patient or, if applicable, the patient’s parent(s)/legal guardian(s), are able and willing to provide informed consent
7. 4. Willingness to attend the study visit schedule and be compliant with the protocol
8. 5. Willing to use highly effective contraception for 6 months post-GT if female patient in the reproductive age range
Exclusion criteria:
1. Prior allogeneic HSCT within 6 months or with evidence of residual cells of donor origin
2. Pregnancy
3. Participation in another interventional clinical trial

sites.f: San Raffaele Hospital – Pediatric Immunohematology Unit
